frames.narration: Events pour in from the stream: 500,000 per second. The ingest worker merges events with the same minute, country, device and campaign into one row with a count and a sum.

The rolled-up rows sit in an in-memory real-time segment, already queryable. When the hour closes, the worker writes an immutable columnar segment with dictionary-encoded columns and bitmaps, and uploads it to deep storage.
The worker records the segment in the catalog with its time range and version, and commits the stream offsets in the same step. After a crash it resumes from them, so no event is counted twice.
An analyst opens a dashboard: events by device for country DE or FR, over the last 6 hours. The query goes to the broker.
The broker asks the catalog which segments overlap the last 6 hours. Of a year of segments, only 6 hourly ones match, and the newest is still in memory on the hot node.
The query is scattered to the hot node that holds those segments. It ORs the bitmaps for DE and FR, groups the surviving rows by device and replies with a few partial sums, not rows.
The analyst widens the range to 90 days. The broker also asks the cold node, which serves older segments from cheaper disks and from deep storage, and is slower.

The broker gathers the partial results, adds the counts and sums from the hot and cold tiers, applies the sort and limit, and sends one small table back. The deadline and row limits kept the query from taking over the cluster.
